moduleTitle: Advanced Use Cases - Module Properties for Realistic Interaction
learningObjectives: Distinguish identifying properties from supported steering parameters.
Validate uniqueness and stability of captured identifiers.
Use documented native Android scrolling configuration.
Separate reusable control configuration from scenario synchronization and outcome assertions.

elements.term: Fix it once, not in every TestCase
elements.description: A reusable Module stores control identification and supported steering configuration. Changes can affect tests that reference it, so validate the affected usages. Not every wait, focus, keyboard or transition behavior is a configurable Module property; some require TCPs, Modules or scenario-specific TestStepValues.

elements.text: Independent maintainability guidance: put a stable reusable control rule in supported shared configuration, and keep scenario-specific actions and assertions explicit. Confirm the actual parameter’s supported level and platform before moving it.

bulletPoints: Shared control configuration can affect multiple usages; validate them.
Use the parameter’s documented level, not a universal Module-placement rule.

elements.description: XScan identifies controls by properties by default. Make Unique can choose additional properties; you can also choose them manually or use another method. Validate that the selected values uniquely identify the target in expected languages, states and layouts.

elements.title: Conditions to investigate
items: A language-specific failure warrants inspecting localized identifiers, layout, application data and target context; it does not prove a text locator is the sole cause.
A changing list warrants inspecting uniqueness and any index-based assumptions.
A different screen size warrants inspecting visibility, scrolling, layout and any coordinate assumptions.
A surrounding UI change warrants inspecting hierarchy and target context along with actual captured properties.

elements.text: A reproduction condition is evidence for investigation, not a guaranteed property diagnosis. Compare the current control tree and selected properties with the failing TestStep and logs.

bulletPoints: Validate actual uniqueness and stability after scanning.
Reproduction conditions guide investigation without proving one locator cause.

elements.description: Use the supported interaction path and verify the required business outcome. If a scenario explicitly depends on focus, confirmation or another action, establish that it occurred; a final stored value alone may not demonstrate the required path. This is a local testing principle, not a claim that every native value-setting operation bypasses user behavior.

elements.title: Documented configuration and explicit actions
items: For Android native controls, Mobile Engine automatically scrolls to find targets. To disable this, add steering parameter ScrollingBehavior=None in the Module Properties tab.
The TapByCoordinates=True TCP is a documented {CLICK} fallback; validate the resulting target and action.
Use supported keyboard Modules/commands for the platform rather than inventing a universal keyboard Module property.
Use explicit readiness waits and supported actions where the scenario requires them; transitions are not all controlled by one Module setting.

elements.text: Native mobile automation does not support Tosca user simulations; the steering guide refers to SendKeys keyboard commands for native interactions. Do not imply that desktop simulation properties automatically apply to native mobile controls.

bulletPoints: Native Android ScrollingBehavior=None disables automatic scrolling.
Validate explicit scenario actions and assertions; native user-simulation support differs from desktop.

examPitfalls.title: Working around a control's behaviour in every TestCase
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Adding the same wait, scroll, or extra tap in each TestCase that touches a particular control.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use supported reusable configuration for a shared control behavior, then validate affected usages. Scenario-specific waits may still need explicit TestSteps.

examPitfalls.title: Trusting the scan's automatic identification unconditionally
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming the properties chosen during scanning are stable, then treating the resulting condition-specific failures as environment problems.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Inspect current control properties, context and logs under the failing condition. A language or layout change alone does not prove one identifier is responsible.

examPitfalls.title: Setting values directly instead of interacting realistically
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Writing a value straight into a control and getting a green TestCase, while the real flow depends on focus, confirmation, or scroll-triggered loading.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: When a scenario explicitly requires interaction events, verify those events and the outcome with supported native actions; do not assume every direct value operation necessarily skips them.

practiceQuiz.scenario: You need to disable the documented automatic scrolling for an Android native Module. Which configuration is documented?

options.text: Add an arbitrary wait to every TestCase.
Add steering parameter ScrollingBehavior=None in the Module Properties tab.
Set a custom TCP named DisableAllScrolling and assume the engine recognizes it.
Image-based identification is mandatory to disable scrolling.

practiceQuiz.hint: Use the supported parameter and documented Module configuration.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The native-control steering guide documents ScrollingBehavior=None at Module level to disable Android automatic scrolling. Invented TCP names and image identification do not implement this documented configuration.

optionExplanations.A: A wait does not configure the documented scrolling switch.
optionExplanations.B: This is the documented native Android Module steering configuration.
optionExplanations.C: An invented custom name is not a supported engine switch.
optionExplanations.D: Disabling scrolling does not require image identification.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Inspection confirms the control is identified by its English label, but the German build changes that label and the locator no longer matches. Which cause does this evidence establish?

options.text: Localised text is participating in how the control is identified.

practiceQuiz.hint: The actual identifying property was inspected, not inferred from language alone.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The confirmed English-label locator no longer matches the localized label. Revise and validate identification; generic language-specific failure alone would require further investigation.

optionExplanations.A: No memory defect is established by the inspected locator mismatch.
optionExplanations.B: The inspected localized label no longer matches the identifying value.
optionExplanations.C: The scenario establishes a label mismatch, not a server address defect.
optionExplanations.D: The scenario establishes a locator cause, not missing reset.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A flow explicitly requires a confirmation action, but a test only checks the resulting stored value and never establishes that confirmation occurred. What coverage gap can remain?

options.text: Direct value setting is not supported on Android.
The stored-value check does not establish that the required confirmation path was exercised.
It always triggers an Appium session restart.
Values set directly are discarded when the keyboard closes.

practiceQuiz.hint: Separate the required interaction path from a final stored value.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A value assertion alone does not establish the required confirmation action. This scenario does not imply all native input operations bypass user behavior.

optionExplanations.A: The scenario does not establish platform-wide unsupported input.
optionExplanations.B: A stored value does not prove the required confirmation path occurred.
optionExplanations.C: No automatic session restart is established.
optionExplanations.D: No automatic value discard is established.

quickRecap.value: Supported reusable Module configuration can affect multiple usages; validate them.
Use the parameter’s documented level; scenario actions may require explicit TestSteps.
Make Unique and manual property selection help identification; validate stability in intended states.
A failure condition guides investigation; inspected locator evidence establishes the cause.
Native Android automatic scrolling can be disabled with ScrollingBehavior=None; native user simulations are not supported.
